top_choice_rationale: P001 rests on a quantitative prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band condition at a magic twist angle) that was tested by experiment and followed by reproduced correlated insulating and superconducting states, a discovery that can be stated in one sentence. The prediction-plus-demonstration split fits three names, and the citation can be worded around the flat bands and observed phases without claiming the pairing mechanism. I weigh the open attribution edges (Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto; Cao, Dean, Young, Yacoby) and twist-angle disorder as wording and credit costs, not as reasons to withhold. P002 is the more mature, cleanly credited fallback but sits close to the 2005 and 2012 precision-measurement prizes; P003 has a harder credit boundary and an unshown simulation advantage but still beats no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented connection to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer (my LaAlO3/SrTiO3 oxide-interface microscopy is adjacent but distinct), nor to Katori, Ye, Bloch, Greiner or Zoller; I share Chalmers with Johansson, who prefers P003, which is a collegial connection only.
